cells.tense: You are sitting here with the pen, writing down what this group is doing.
cells.ask: Promise one person that today you will show them the exact moment a pattern first appeared.
cells.core: You catch the repeated beat before anyone names it, and you say it in plain words so the others can move. That is the harvest here — a pattern recognized and handed over, so it stops running the room from under the table. People hear your description as a description, not as their own assumption, and that is why it lands. The pull of what might be felt next is what keeps you at the table; the freeing is the point, not the analysis. What this costs to keep is that nobody thanks you for seeing clearly in the moment it happens, and the hours you spend reading the room are hours no one counts.

cells.tense: You are racing ahead to the conclusion while the other people are still on the setup.
cells.ask: In your next meeting, let the other person finish before you add anything, and speak only after they stop.
cells.core: The analysis finishes in you long before anyone else has the first page read, and the gap turns into pressure. What was going to free these people into new thinking arrives as a verdict from next week, so they brace instead of open. The thing you want them to see moves further away the harder you push it toward them. The other side of this is structure that serves what it organizes — something clear and reliable, where what you say makes sense to the people hearing it and not only to you. Bring the writing back to now and the cutting stops feeling like a threat.

cells.tense: You saw the pattern and stopped putting it into words for the people around you.
cells.ask: Write one thing you noticed this week and read it aloud to one person without softening it.
cells.core: When this works, you take what you have noticed and set it in front of the group, and they can pick it up or leave it. You keep seeing it; what has gone quiet is the handoff. You stay near the table and let the same old story repeat, half in, half out, and what you see turns into private commentary instead of something shared. That is the shape of the shortfall: the ability is there and the offering isn't. What is missing is not more analysis. It is the walking across toward the people who would use it. One person, one thing you already see, said plainly, is the way back.

cells.tense: You are already running the analysis for this group while calling it something that happened on its own.
cells.ask: Name one decision you made for the group this past week and say out loud that it was yours.
cells.core: The pattern you spot gets handed over with a person behind it, so the group can see where the thought came from and argue with it if they want. What moves through you now has no such mark on it — what gets passed along and what gets let stand all going through you and coming out as just how things are. Underneath the finished analysis sits a simpler kind of recognition, the felt sense that this reading belongs to you and to them at once. Saying so is not a new job laid on top. It is putting a person behind what the table already treats as fact.
